lots.key_photo_findings: Signature in dark paint at lower left reads 'H.K. ROOKE' (photo 3; the researcher said lower right, but the close-up shows it at the bottom left beside the slip). The frame label reads 'FRAMNAES NORWAY / H.K. ROOKE R.B.A.' (photo 4). Framnaes is on the Sognefjord at Balestrand, a known haunt of British painters around 1900. The researcher reads the artist as Harry Kingsley Rooke; from memory the RBA painter with these initials may be Herbert Kerr Rooke (1872-1944), a British marine painter, but I could not check this with any source, so treat the attribution as unconfirmed. The back shows an old canvas on a keyed stretcher with a later dust cover and wire, consistent with an early 20th century painting.
lots.condition: Surface grime and a dull varnish on the canvas. The gilt slip is dirty and stained along the bottom edge. Oak frame has minor knocks at the corners. No tears or losses seen in the photos. It would likely benefit from a surface clean.
